title: Fix crash on closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.

requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.intent: A [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly must build cleanly and still get a generated resolver.

functional.text: The generator does not throw when a member's type is a closed generic struct or record struct defined in a referenced assembly.
The analyzer does not throw for the same member types.
The compiling assembly gets its generated resolver, as it does when the generic type is declared in the same project.

nonFunctional.text: A failure of the generator or analyzer must not pass silently as a build warning that leaves the assembly without a resolver. (inferred)
Behaviour for generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same project does not change. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (for example a field of type Ref.Pair<int, string>) does not throw IndexOutOfRangeException or any other exception in the source generator.
The same holds when the referenced generic type is a record struct, and when it is used as a property or field.
The build produces no generator-crash warning (CS8785 or similar) for these member types.

expectedBehaviours: Running the MessagePack analyzers on a [MessagePackObject] type with a member whose type is a closed generic struct or record struct from a referenced assembly does not throw.
No analyzer-crash diagnostic (AD0001) is reported for these member types.
The analyzer reports only the MsgPack diagnostics it would report for an equivalent same-project type, or none.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a referenced-assembly closed generic struct member finds no AD0001 and no unexpected MsgPack diagnostics.
An analyzer test covers the record struct variant in the same way.

The generated output matches what is produced when the generic struct is declared in the same project, apart from type location details such as namespaces.
Serializing and deserializing an instance through the generated resolver round-trips the member value.

expectedBehaviours: A generator or analyzer exception does not end as only a build warning while the assembly silently ships without a generated resolver.

story.what: TypeCollector now checks every analyzer diagnostic before reporting it and drops any whose location is not in source inside the current compilation. Two places that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly, the property BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic and the field MemberNeedsKey diagnostic, now return a null location when the member has no source declaration. Separately, the MsgPack014 filter in the analyzer now matches nullable-annotated reference type arguments instead of not-annotated ones. New tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image and check that a closed generic struct or record struct from it gives no diagnostics and that the resolver is generated.
story.why: When a member's type was a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, the generator and the analyzer threw IndexOutOfRangeException because the struct's members have no syntax. The crash surfaced only as AD0001/CS8785 warnings, and the assembly ended up without its generated resolver (MP-2283).

Uses the null-safe location lookups instead of DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].
The nullable-reference-type formatter filter now matches NullableAnnotation.Annotated.
New helper. Runs the verifier against a metadata-only reference, then checks the generator's diagnostics and the resolver hint name.

findings.title: MsgPack014 filter reversed from NotAnnotated to Annotated
findings.detail: In SymbolStartAction, the MsgPack014 (NullableReferenceTypeFormatter) query now selects IMessagePackFormatter<T> type arguments whose NullableAnnotation is Annotated, where it used to select NotAnnotated ones. The diagnostic message says "Implement IMessagePackFormatter<{0}?> (with nullable annotation)". So every formatter that already implements the annotated interface correctly now gets a warning telling it to do what it already does. Formatters that really lack the annotation are no longer flagged. Projects that treat warnings as errors will break on correct code, and existing MsgPack014 tests should fail. The requirement does not ask for this change, and nothing in the crash fix depends on it.

findings.title: Location filter also drops diagnostics owned by the current compilation
findings.detail: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only when Location.IsInSource is true. Any diagnostic created with a null location becomes Location.None and is dropped, even when the problem is in a type declared in the project being built. GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null for any property whose declaring syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. A record positional property is declared by a ParameterSyntax, so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for a same-project record parameter with a null key is now silently discarded. Before the change it at least surfaced as an analyzer crash. The generator then goes on with neither an int nor a string key. The same applies to any other diagnostic whose location lookup returns null for a source type. Requirement item N1 says problems must not pass silently. The filter should drop only locations that are in another syntax tree or in metadata, and should fall back to the containing type or member location for same-compilation symbols.

findings.title: Generated resolver content and round-trip for referenced generic struct unchecked
findings.detail: For a closed generic type from metadata, CollectGeneric now generates a formatter for the referenced type definition inside the consuming assembly. The new tests skip the generated-source check and only assert that the resolver hint name exists. No snapshot shows the resolver and formatter output matching what a same-project declaration produces. No runtime test round-trips such a member through the generated resolver. F3 expects both, so a resolver with a wrong or missing registration would still pass.

findings.title: No safeguard against generator exceptions passing silently as warnings
findings.detail: The change fixes only the two IndexOutOfRange sites reached in the reported scenario. Nothing makes a generator or analyzer exception on other unusual input visible as an error, so the assembly can still ship without a resolver behind nothing more than a CS8785 warning. One remaining example is the hard cast to BaseMethodDeclarationSyntax in GetParameterListLocation, which fails on a record primary constructor. N1 asks that such failures not pass silently, for example by catching exceptions in the collector and reporting an error diagnostic.
